name: Holidays at the Disneyland Resort
summary: Disney confirms Holidays at the Disneyland Resort for November 13, 2026–January 6, 2027. Both parks offer included seasonal entertainment and ride overlays; the festival food and optional extras cost more.
h1: Holidays at the Disneyland Resort: what is included, and the two weeks to book instead of Christmas
title: Holidays at the Disneyland Resort
description: Confirmed Disneyland holiday dates for 2026–27, including Festival of Holidays, four ride overlays, parade, fireworks and World of Color.

typicalWindow.hours: Every operating day from November 13, 2026 through January 6, 2027; showtimes, ride availability and food marketplace hours vary by date. Check Disney’s daily calendar.

pricing.asOf: prior holiday cycle; 2026–27 menu not announced as of September 26, 2026
pricing.cheapestNights: The ten days before Thanksgiving, and the first full week of January once the New Year crowd has gone home
pricing.priciestNights: The stretch from the week before Christmas through New Year's Day, which is the most expensive and most crowded period of the Disneyland Resort year
notes: The 2026–27 holiday program is included with regular admission and a same-day park reservation. Marketplace food, merchandise and optional extras cost more.
The range above is not an admission price. It is what a Festival of Holidays marketplace item costs, which along with merchandise is the only spend the season genuinely adds.
Disneyland Resort has not run a hard-ticket holiday party in recent seasons, so there is no paid route into a quieter version of this.
Ticket prices are date-based and the late-December dates sit in the highest tier, which is the closest thing the season has to a price.
Anaheim hotel rates in the last two weeks of December are the highest of the year, and the walkable independent hotels lose most of their usual price advantage.

whatYouGet: “it’s a small world” Holiday and its evening façade projections at Disneyland Park.
Haunted Mansion Holiday, carried from the Halloween season into the holiday program.
Luigi’s Joy to the Whirl and Mater’s Jingle Jamboree in Cars Land.
A Christmas Fantasy Parade and “Believe…In Holiday Magic” Fireworks at Disneyland Park, subject to the daily entertainment calendar.
World of Color – Season of Light at Disney California Adventure.
Disney Festival of Holidays and Disney ¡Viva Navidad! at Disney California Adventure, November 13–January 6; marketplace food is an extra purchase.
Wintertime Enchantment at Sleeping Beauty’s Winter Castle and festive décor throughout the resort.
whatYouDont: Any relief from the crowds. The week between Christmas and New Year is the busiest of the Disneyland Resort year, and in most recent seasons the resort has reached capacity and stopped admitting guests on at least one of those days. A valid ticket does not guarantee entry once that happens.
The standard versions of “it’s a small world” or Haunted Mansion while their holiday overlays operate; check each attraction’s daily schedule.

A hard-ticket alternative. There is no Disneyland equivalent of Mickey's Very Merry Christmas Party, which means there is no way to buy your way into a less crowded evening the way you can in Florida.
Guaranteed fireworks, parade, or snowfall. All three are weather-dependent, and winter wind cancels the Disneyland Park fireworks noticeably more often than summer weather does.
Short queues guaranteed on the holiday ride overlays. Waits vary by date and should be checked in the Disneyland app.
A cheap trip. The tickets cost the same as any other peak date, but late-December lodging, parking, and flights into Southern California all price at their annual highs at once.

verdict.short: The best value of any seasonal offering at either resort, because all of it is included with a normal ticket. Go before Thanksgiving or in early January; the last two weeks of December are brutal.
worthItIf: You want the most heavily decorated version of an American Disney park without paying for an event ticket on top of admission.
You can travel after the November 13 opening and before Thanksgiving, or during the first days of January through January 6.
Your group cares more about parades, decoration, shows, and food than about ride count.
You have visited Disneyland Resort in another season and want a genuinely different park rather than the same one with a tree in it.
You are eating your way through the trip. Festival of Holidays is the largest food event Disney California Adventure runs all year and it is free to walk into.
skipIf: Your only available dates are the last two weeks of December and crowds bother anyone in your group. That period is the hardest stretch of the year to enjoy at this resort, and no amount of planning fixes it.
You specifically want the standard versions of “it’s a small world” or Haunted Mansion during their holiday overlay period.
You are optimizing only for rides per day. Holiday entertainment, overlays and crowds can change wait and walkway patterns.
You are price-sensitive on lodging. This is the one season where the Anaheim hotel advantage over Orlando largely disappears.
You need reliable weather for an outdoor-heavy plan. December and January are Southern California's wettest months and a rained-out day takes the parade and fireworks with it.

strategy.heading: The two windows that make this work
body: The confirmed 2026–27 program runs November 13 through January 6. For quieter dates, compare weekdays before Thanksgiving and the first days of January, then check Disney’s daily calendar.

Disney confirms the 2026–27 holiday program from November 13 through January 6. The daily calendar, rather than the season span alone, is the source for individual shows and attractions on a particular date.
The confirmed season runs through January 6, 2027, so early January remains an option for holiday offerings. Verify individual showtimes and attraction status before treating every day as identical.

The one caveat on January: it is the start of refurbishment season. Disney does its heaviest maintenance work in the first quarter, so a January visit that gets you an empty park often gets you two or three headliners behind walls. Check the closure list before you commit.

strategy.heading: Christmas week, if you genuinely have no choice
body: Plan for capacity closures rather than for wait times. On peak December days the resort has closed one or both parks to further entry, and once that happens a valid ticket does not get you in. Being through the gates before nine in the morning is not a tactic for beating queues here; it is how you guarantee you get into the park at all.

Park hopping is the second trap. Hopping opens later in the day, and on capacity days the park you want to hop into may be closed to hoppers even when it is open to guests who started there. Pick your morning park deliberately and treat the hop as optional rather than as the plan.

For the parade, watch from Frontierland or the walkway toward "it's a small world" rather than from Main Street or the hub. The hub fills 60 to 90 minutes ahead on peak days, the outer stretches fill in the last 20 minutes, and the parade is the same parade.

Give up on doing everything. On a peak December day a realistic target is four or five attractions, the parade, and one nighttime show, and a family that accepts that in advance has a far better time than one that arrives with a list of twelve.

strategy.heading: Festival of Holidays and what it actually costs
body: Disney California Adventure's Festival of Holidays is included with admission; the food is not, and marketplace items ran $6 to $15 each as of July 2026. Two adults sharing five plates make a full lunch out of it for the price of a mediocre quick-service meal.

The non-obvious timing: the marketplaces are at their quietest between roughly eleven in the morning and one in the afternoon, because at that hour everyone else is in Cars Land or on Pixar Pier. They jam from about half past one onwards, which is precisely when the ride waits dip. Running the opposite pattern to the crowd gets you both.

A coupon booklet covering a fixed number of items is sold each season. It only pays for itself if you commit to the full count, and two adults sharing plates almost never get there. Buy per item unless you have counted.
Disney ¡Viva Navidad! runs November 13–January 6. Its street party is advertised for Saturdays and Sundays; check the entertainment calendar for exact performance times.

strategy.heading: Choose the confirmed holiday ride overlays
body: Disney’s 2026 holiday page lists “it’s a small world” Holiday, Haunted Mansion Holiday, Luigi’s Joy to the Whirl and Mater’s Jingle Jamboree. It does not list a Jingle Cruise overlay.
The “it’s a small world” façade projections are a separate outdoor experience that you can enjoy without joining the ride queue.
Check the Disneyland app for each ride’s daily operating hours and any refurbishment. The holiday program dates do not guarantee every attraction every day.
Cars Land adds two seasonal ride versions at DCA, useful if your group wants holiday rides in both parks.

strategy.heading: Evenings, and the moment the whole season is built around
body: The snowfall on Main Street after the Disneyland Park fireworks is what the entire overlay is designed to end on, and it happens whether or not you are standing anywhere useful. Being on Main Street for it is worth more than being in the best fireworks viewing spot.

The practical compromise: watch the fireworks from the walkway toward "it's a small world" rather than the hub. You give up the castle projections, you gain the lit small world facade behind you, a fraction of the crowd, and an exit that is not the single worst pedestrian jam at the resort.

At Disney California Adventure the holiday version of the Paradise Bay show is the better use of an evening than a second night of fireworks, and it is far easier to get a viewing spot for. It also finishes closer to park close, which means the walk out is spread rather than simultaneous.
Sleeping Beauty's Winter Castle is lit each evening and photographs badly from directly in front. The angle from the Frontierland side of the hub is better, quieter, and available.

food.note: Festival of Holidays returns November 13, 2026–January 6, 2027, but Disney labels its 2026–27 Foodie Guide coming soon as of September 26. The items below are examples from a prior holiday cycle and must not be treated as the current menu or current prices.

items.name: Holiday Slider with Braised Beef
items.verdict: The most filling thing in the festival for the money and the easiest sell to anyone who is not enthusiastic about small plates.

items.name: Pozole
items.verdict: Better than it needs to be, and the only marketplace item that works as an actual meal on a cold evening.

items.name: Latke with Applesauce
items.verdict: Small, reliably good, and the fastest-moving line of the marketplaces most days.

items.name: Seasonal Dessert Flight
items.verdict: Three small sweets for the price of one dessert elsewhere in the park, and the item most worth splitting between four people.

items.name: Korean-style Short Rib Bowl
items.verdict: A permanent restaurant running a festival menu, which means real seating and a shorter line than the marketplace stalls a few feet away.

faqs.q: Is the Disneyland holiday season included with a regular ticket?
faqs.a: Yes, all of it. Every ride overlay, the parade, both nighttime shows, the castle lighting, the Main Street snowfall, and entry to the Festival of Holidays marketplaces come with ordinary admission. Disneyland Resort runs no hard-ticket holiday party, which makes this the best-value seasonal offering at either American Disney resort by a wide margin.

faqs.q: When do the holiday decorations go up and come down at Disneyland?
faqs.a: Disney confirms Holidays at the Disneyland Resort from November 13, 2026 through January 6, 2027. Check the daily calendar for individual decorations, entertainment and attraction operations; the season dates do not guarantee every offering each day.

faqs.q: Is there a Christmas party ticket at Disneyland like Mickey's Very Merry?
faqs.a: No. Disneyland Resort has not run a hard-ticket holiday party in recent seasons, so there is no paid route into a quieter evening. That is a genuine advantage on price and a genuine disadvantage on crowds, and it is the main structural difference between the two resorts at Christmas.

faqs.q: When is the least crowded time to see the holidays at Disneyland?
faqs.a: Consider weekdays from the November 13 opening until Thanksgiving, or the first days of January through January 6, 2027. These are planning windows rather than crowd guarantees; check park reservations, hours and refurbishments for your dates.

faqs.q: Does Disneyland close its gates at Christmas?
faqs.a: It has, in most recent seasons, on at least one day in the week between Christmas and New Year. Once a park hits capacity it stops admitting further guests, including guests holding valid tickets and reservations, and it reopens entry only as people leave. If you are visiting in that window, be through the gates before nine in the morning.

A food festival at Disney California Adventure that runs alongside the season and is included with admission, with marketplaces serving dishes drawn from a rotating set of winter holiday traditions. The food costs extra, at $6 to $15 per item as of July 2026. It also carries the Viva Navidad street party, which is the best live entertainment at either park in December.

faqs.q: Can I ride the normal "it's a small world" during the holidays?
faqs.a: During the holiday overlay, the attraction operates as “it’s a small world” Holiday rather than its regular version. Disney lists it in the November 13–January 6 holiday program; check the daily calendar for operating hours.
